synopsis: COLMAP is described as a widely used free, open-source structure-from-motion tool that recovers camera positions and a three-dimensional point cloud from photographs; this is one part of the broader process of producing a usable virtual site [f13144, f13146]. Its reconstruction guidance requires good texture, similar illumination, substantial image overlap, at least three observations of each object, and genuinely different camera positions rather than pure rotation [f3799, f4025, f13147]. Textureless scenes, high dynamic range, glare, shadows and reflective surfaces are identified as reconstruction risks; numerous near-identical video frames cannot substitute for different viewpoints, and video downsampling is suggested [f3800, f4040, f4027, f13149]. An on-road EUVS benchmark required more than 800 hours of COLMAP computation, while the glossary reports more than 300 additional hours of manual selection; these figures are not a direct estimate of job-site digital-twin costs [f3898, f13150]. The booklet also names COLMAP as photogrammetry software and includes quarry drone-survey examples, but the supplied facts provide no quantified quarry reconstruction cost [f16003, f3898].
